This mentality drives me crazy. I feel I must push back a bit here:

Back "in the day": Yes, you could work on 1 income, BUT ...:

  1. you only had 1 car per family (1 extra car: ~$500 / month)
  2. you didn't have 2+ cell phones ($125 / month)
  3. you didn't a cable TV bill ($100 / month)
  4. you didn't eat out except on very special occasions. If you had to eat out, you brought a brown bag lunch. ($ 400 / month)
  5. you didn't eat processed / expensive pre packaged meals, drink sodas, etc. ($200 / month)
  6. you didn't have a washer, dryer, dishwasher, A/C (cost + electric cost: $200 / month, depending on where you live...)
  7. you didn't commute long distances and live in 'bedroom communities' ($200 / month)
  8. you didn't take expensive vacations to Hawaii or Cancun. ($200 / month)
  9. you didn't put your kids in daycare ($400 / month)
  10. you didn't have credit cards or other consumer debt. ($100 / month in interest..)
  11. you offset expenses by having a garden, having chickens, by mending clothing, by fixing your own stuff when it breaks. ($50/month)

My numbers may be high or low depending on the family, but roughly speaking, what I outlined there is ~$30,000 year.

Except for items #1 (we have 2 older vehicles), #2 (cell phones) and #6 (modern appliances), we do all of the above. This makes us "weird" in the eyes of modern society. But, we live extremely comfortably on 1 income. Over the years as the 1 income has grown, we have increased our savings rate and not our expenditure rate. We won't need to work beyond ~55.

Yeah - taxes are too high and our standard of living is dropping thanks to bad domestic and foreign policies.

But, don't think you can compare the modern consumeristic lifestyle with the way things were back when it was the norm to have 1 full time spouse at home.
